title: Hawaij root vegetable stew with whipped fenugreek

source.title: Yotam Ottolenghi's warming winter vegetable recipes

instructions: Whipped fenugreek, at least 2 hours ahead: soak the ground fenugreek in 250ml boiling water for 2 hours or overnight. Pour off the liquid, add 1 tbsp water and whisk the spongy fenugreek for about 10 minutes until pale like mayonnaise. Blitz with the chilli, spring onion, 10g coriander, 1½ tbsp lemon juice, ¼ tsp salt and 3 tbsp water until smooth.
Hawaij: toast the coriander and cumin seeds, peppercorns and cloves, grind finely with the cardamom seeds, and stir in the turmeric.

Cut the onion into 8 wedges, crush the garlic, grate the ginger, peel and coarsely grate the tomatoes, and chop 30g coriander. Peel the swede, parsnips, carrots and potatoes and cut into 3cm chunks, parsnips into quarters lengthways, carrots into 1½cm angled slices.
Heat the oil in a large pan over a medium-high heat. Cook the onion for about 4 minutes, until softened. Add the garlic, ginger, tomato paste and hawaij and cook for 30 seconds, until fragrant.

Add the tomatoes, two-thirds of the chopped coriander and 2 tbsp water and cook for about 5 minutes, until the tomatoes have cooked down. Add 650ml water, the sugar, the root vegetables and 1¾ tsp salt, bring to the boil, then simmer on medium for about 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and thick.
Stir in half the whipped fenugreek, cook 10 minutes more, then stir in the rest of the coriander. Serve in bowls with the remaining fenugreek drizzled over, more coriander and the yoghurt.
